steps.title: Anesthetize mouse with Avertin
steps.instruction: Inject the mouse intraperitoneally with 2.5 % (v/v) Avertin solution.

steps.title: Perfuse mouse intracardially
steps.instruction: Using a peristaltic pump set to 2–3 mL/min, perform intracardiac perfusion in the following order: (i) 8 mL ice‑cold PBS to flush blood, (ii) 20 mL 0.5 mg/mL Sulfo‑NHS‑biotin for luminal biotinylation, (iii) 10 mL 50 mM Tris‑PBS to quench unreacted biotin. Expose the chest cavity, make a small incision in the right atrium for drainage, insert the perfusion needle into the left ventricle without puncturing the wall, and start the pump immediately, switching solutions as indicated.

steps.title: Extract brain into BSA/PI
steps.instruction: Open the skull with surgical scissors, gently remove the brain with forceps, and place it in cold 1 % BSA + 1× protease inhibitor (PI) in PBS on ice.

steps.title: Place tissue in BSA/PI
steps.instruction: Place the hemibrain in 0.5 mL of 1 % BSA + 1× PI in a 60 mm Petri dish on ice.

steps.title: Mince tissue
steps.instruction: Mince the brain tissue into ~1 mm³ pieces using a razor blade.

steps.title: Transfer to Dounce
steps.instruction: Transfer the minced tissue into a 7 mL Dounce homogenizer on ice using a pre‑cut 1,000 µL pipette tip.

steps.title: Wash and add remaining tissue
steps.instruction: Wash the razor blade and Petri dish with 1 mL 1 % BSA + 1× PI and add this wash to the Dounce homogenizer.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue
steps.instruction: Dounce gently until just homogenized (≈20 strokes, very little twisting) with no visible tissue chunks; keep the Dounce on ice throughout.

steps.title: Add dextran solution
steps.instruction: Transfer the homogenate to a 15 mL conical tube containing 10 mL chilled 32 % dextran.

steps.title: Wash Dounce into dextran
steps.instruction: Wash the Dounce homogenizer with 1 mL 1 % BSA + 1× PI and add this wash to the same 15 mL tube with dextran.

steps.title: Mix homogenate with dextran
steps.instruction: Invert the tube repeatedly until the tissue homogenate is fully mixed with the dextran solution.

steps.title: Density centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the dextran‑brain mixture at 4,400 × g, 4 °C for 25 min with slow deceleration.

steps.title: Remove supernatant layers
steps.instruction: Aspirate the top myelin layer and the middle parenchymal cell layer, leaving the microvessel pellet at the bottom.

steps.title: Pre‑wet strainer
steps.instruction: Pre‑wet the mesh of a 40 µm cell strainer placed atop a 50 mL conical tube with 5 mL 1 % BSA.

steps.title: Load pellet onto strainer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the microvessel pellet in 1 mL 1 % BSA + 1× PI and apply the suspension to the pre‑wet 40 µm strainer.

steps.title: Wash microvessels with PBS
steps.instruction: Gently wash the retained microvessels by passing 30 mL cold PBS through the strainer.

steps.title: Collect microvessels with BSA wash
steps.instruction: Invert the filter onto a new 50 mL conical tube and wash with 20 mL 1 % BSA; ensure no visible microvessels remain on the strainer.

steps.title: Pellet microvessels
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the collected suspension at 2,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C with slow deceleration.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant without disturbing the microvessel pellet.

steps.title: Lyse microvessels in RIPA
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 200 µL RIPA buffer supplemented with 1× PI, transfer to a 1.5 mL low‑protein‑retention microcentrifuge tube, and store lysates at –20 °C or –80 °C (pause point).

steps.title: Sonicate microvessel lysate
steps.instruction: Sonicate the lysate on ice in RIPA + 1× PI using a Qsonica sonicator set to 50 % amplitude, 10 s on/30 s off, for 3 cycles.

steps.title: Clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sonicated lysate at 13,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C and retain the supernatant.

steps.title: Determine protein concentration
steps.instruction: Measure the protein concentration of the supernatant using a BCA assay.

steps.title: Enrich biotinylated proteins
steps.instruction: Dilute 1 mg of each sample to a total volume of 300 µL in RIPA + 1× PI, add 70 µL streptavidin magnetic beads, and incubate at 4 °C overnight with end‑over‑end rotation.

steps.title: Wash beads
steps.instruction: The next day, wash the beads once with 200 µL 50 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 7.5) at room temperature, then twice rapidly with 200 µL 2 M urea in 50 mM Tris (pH 7.5) using a magnetic rack.

steps.title: On‑bead reduction and digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the beads with 80 µL 2 M urea in 50 mM Tris containing 1 mM DTT and 0.4 µg trypsin/Lys‑C at 25 °C for 1 h while shaking at 300 rpm.

steps.title: Collect on‑bead digest
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a new low‑binding tube.

steps.title: Wash beads and combine digests
steps.instruction: Wash the beads two times with 60 µL 2 M urea in 50 mM Tris, combine these washes with the previously collected supernatant.

steps.title: Reduce peptides
steps.instruction: Add 4.1 µL of 200 mM DTT to 200 µL of solution to achieve 4 mM final DTT; incubate 30 min at 300 rpm shaking.

steps.title: Alkylate cysteines
steps.instruction: Add 5.2 µL of 400 mM iodoacetamide (IAA) to 204.1 µL solution to reach 10 mM final IAA; incubate 45 min in the dark at 300 rpm shaking.

steps.title: Overnight trypsin digestion
steps.instruction: Add an additional 0.5 µg trypsin/Lys‑C (2.5 µL of 0.2 µg/µL stock) and digest overnight at 37 °C with shaking.

steps.title: Acidify peptide solution
steps.instruction: Add 2.1 µL formic acid to 212 µL peptide solution to reach 1 % (v/v) formic acid.

steps.title: Desalt peptides on C18
steps.instruction: Using BioPureSPN mini C18 columns: (a) Wash columns with 200 µL methanol, then equilibrate twice with 200 µL solvent A (0.1 % FA in LC‑MS‑grade water); (b) Load the peptide sample and centrifuge; (c) Wash four times with 200 µL solvent A, centrifuging each time; (d) Elute twice with 75 µL solvent B (0.1 % FA in 80 % LC‑MS‑grade acetonitrile) into the same low‑binding tube. Perform all centrifugation steps at 50 × g for 1 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Dry peptide eluate
steps.instruction: Dry the combined eluates in a vacuum concentrator.

steps.title: Reconstitute peptides
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the dried peptides in 10 µL solvent A (0.1 % FA in LC‑MS‑grade water) for LC‑MS/MS analysis.

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS acquisition
steps.instruction: Perform LC‑MS/MS using a Q Exactive HF‑X coupled to an UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano system. Load peptides onto a C18 column and separate at 300 nL/min with a 120 min gradient: 0‑18 min 96 % A + 4 % Y, 18‑90 min 70 % A + 30 % Y, 90‑105 min 60 % A + 40 % Y, 105‑120 min 4 % A + 96 % Y (A = 0.1 % FA in water, Y = 0.1 % FA in acetonitrile). Acquire full MS scans at 60,000 resolution, AGC target 3 × 10⁶, max IT 20 ms, m/z 300‑1650. Acquire MS² scans at 15,000 resolution, AGC target 1 × 10⁵, max IT 54 ms, loop count 15, TopN 15, isolation window 1.4 m/z, first mass 100 m/z, NCE 28, charge exclusion of unassigned, 1, 6‑8, >8, peptide match preferred, exclude isotopes on, dynamic exclusion 45 s.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol (or parts of it) has been used and validated in the following research article(s): • Shi et al. [4]. Glycocalyx dysregulation promotes blood-brain barrier dysfunction in ageing and disease. Nature. (Extended Data Figure 4A–F). Key validations using brain section imaging, western blot, GO term enrichment analysis of identified proteins, detection of known luminal candidates, and differential expression analysis between experimental groups are also depicted in Figure 1 .
